title: Beef Birria Queso Tacos with Consommé
description: Chef John's birria tacos recipe pan-fries tortillas filled with a delicious mixture of shredded beef and gooey cheese. Serve with consommé for dipping.
ingredients: 2 cups reserved sauce from Beef Birria recipe
3 tablespoons reserved beef fat from Beef Birria recipe, or more as needed
2 cups freshly grated Monterey Jack cheese
4 tablespoons chopped white onion, or to taste
4 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro, or to taste

steps.text: To make the consommé: Stir beef birria sauce, chicken broth, carrots, celery, and cabbage together in a saucepan over high heat. Bring to a simmer, then reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer, occasionally brushing the caramelized bits (fond) off the side with the hot liquid, until vegetables are nice and tender and consommé has reached the desired consistency, about 20 minutes. Reduce the heat to low and keep hot while you prepare the tacos.

To make the tacos: Heat some reserved beef fat in a large skillet over medium heat until melted. Add two tortillas and flip with a spatula until generously coated in fat. Toast briefly until golden brown, then cover with Monterey Jack cheese and some shredded beef.
Drizzle each taco with about 1 tablespoon consommé liquid, then top with some white onion and cilantro.

Fold tacos in half and press gently. Continue to cook, flipping back and forth, until browned and crispy, 2 to 3 minutes. Transfer to a plate and repeat to make remaining tacos, adding more fat if necessary.
Ladle consommé into a bowl and garnish with any remaining white onion and cilantro. Squeeze lime wedges into consommé and serve with tacos.

video.description: In this video, Chef John shares his take on the world's most trendy taco recipe - Beef Birria Queso Tacos with Consomé. He starts by making a savory consomé using the reserved sauce from his Beef Birria recipe along with chicken broth, carrots, celery, and cabbage. Then, he assembles the tacos by toasting corn tortillas in beef fat, adding Monterey Jack cheese and shredded beef, and drizzling with consomé liquid before topping with white onion and cilantro. The tacos are cooked until browned and crispy, and served with the consomé garnished with onions, cilantro, and lime wedges. Chef John's tips include shredding the beef finely for better absorption of the liquid, shredding your own cheese, and using beef broth instead of chicken broth.
